text:
jess-people-ops: Hey everyone — quick heads up: today were launching a pilot called the "Dependency Care Credit" for 2026. Its a small stipend to help cover care costs for dependents (elderly care, ADA-related caregiving, long-term child care beyond subsidized options). Details below and a short FAQ. Please read and flag any major blockers by EOD Fri :spiral_calendar: 

jess-people-ops: TL;DR: $500/yr per eligible employee, paid as a taxable stipend via payroll in two installments. Pilot runs Jan2026 through Dec2026. Opt-in required via People Ops form. Eligibility is broad but region-specific limits apply (see EU/UK note). Internal doc: https://redwood.internal/hr/dependency-care-credit

aaron-people-ops: Quick note: this is not PTO. Its reimbursement-style stipend for things like in-home caregivers, respite care, home modification equipment, transportation to appointments. Not for regular household bills.

emily-hr: Eligibility quick checklist (summary):
```
- Employee status: full-time or part-time >0.6 FTE
- Employed during at least 6 months of pilot year
- Dependent types: child under 18, adult dependent with documented need, elderly parent receiving regular care
- Cannot double-dip with regional caregiver subsidies (see EU exceptions)
```

matt-cto: Thanks — who needs to sign off on payroll integration? Id like it in before the first payment run in Feb.

payroll-bot: @jess-people-ops Payroll integration checklist created: `PR-2409`. Next payroll cutoff: 2026-02-15.

jess-people-ops: @matt-cto payroll team (cc @payroll-bot) will handle config. Aaron and I already scoped tax treatment with finance for US/Canada. EU/UK team needs local tax vetting.

luis-eu-ops: In EU well need a country-by-country note. Spain and Germany might treat as taxable income; France may require different reporting. I can coordinate with our local counsel next week.

aaron-people-ops: FAQ excerpt for managers (paste-ready):
- Q: Is this available retroactively? A: No, payments start Feb, pilot applies to expenses dated Jan 1, 2026 onward.
- Q: Does this impact benefits eligibility? A: No, its additive and does not change health or leave entitlements.
- Q: How to claim? A: Upload receipts to the People Ops form and choose stipend payout or reimbursement.

jess-people-ops: Example receipts accepted: invoices from care providers, bank statements showing payment to certified caregivers, invoices for home modifications. Not accepted: rent, utilities, school tuition (unless specifically documented as care services).

emily-hr: Were preparing a 20-min all-hands + AMA next Wed at 10am PT to walk through the pilot. Link & calendar invite to follow.

matt-cto: Sounds good. Any budget cap per team?

aaron-people-ops: Company-wide cap: funds allocated for pilot cover up to 1,200 employees. If opt-ins exceed budget, well prorate based on date of opt-in. We dont expect to hit that, but want transparency.

luis-eu-ops: Also: request local HR to add a short line in offer letters in EU to mention pilot availability (so new hires know they can opt-in once eligible).

jess-people-ops: Action items: 
- People Ops: finalize form + receipts flow (due 2026-01-20) — @aaron-people-ops
- Payroll: set up PR-2409 and tax codes (due 2026-02-05) — @payroll-bot
- EU/UK counsel: confirm tax treatment by 2026-01-28 — @luis-eu-ops
- Eng managers: remind teams about AMA and share this thread if you have direct reports who might use it

aaron-people-ops: If anyone sees immediate compliance red flags for specific countries, DM me.

matt-cto: Appreciate the clarity. Will share in infra-all channel after AMA.

jess-people-ops: Thanks team — leave emoji if youre interested in joining the pilot cohort planning call next Tue (9am PT). :raised_hands: :heart:

luis-eu-ops: :raised_hands:
